No FET028 gripper-site authoring found under /World/AssetRoot/Asset.

FIX: Author one Xform prim per grasp point. Most parallel-jaw
grippers have ONE site at the grasp center between the finger
pads. Place the prim under a stable parent (the gripper base
link) so it translates with the end-effector, and translate it
to the grasp center in local coordinates.

The prim must declare:
  - a discovery marker (spec-canonical socketType OR IsaacSiteAPI)
  - child BasisCurves 'gripper_forward_axis' (approach direction)
  - child BasisCurves 'gripper_grip_line'    (between finger pad tips)
  - custom float 'gripper_maxOpening' (max jaw separation, METERS)

TEMPLATE -- paste under your gripper base prim, edit the
translate / maxOpening / curve points to match your asset:

    def Xform "gripper_01" (
        prepend apiSchemas = ["IsaacSiteAPI"]
    )
    {
        # Spec-canonical discovery (preferred, OpenUSD-compatible)
        token simready:attactment:socketType = "Gripper"

        # Isaac runtime metadata (recommended)
        string isaac:Description = "Parallel-jaw grasp center"

        # Max jaw opening between the two pads, in METERS
        custom float gripper_maxOpening = 0.085
        # Rated payload in kg (optional, used by FET028 to size
        # the test object mass)
        custom float gripper_maxPayload = 5.0

        # Translate to grasp center in local parent coords
        double3 xformOp:translate = (0, 0, 0.16)
        uniform token[] xformOpOrder = ["xformOp:translate"]

        # Approach direction: from grasp center along close-in path
        def BasisCurves "gripper_forward_axis"
        {
            point3f[] points = [(0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 0.05)]
            int[] curveVertexCounts = [2]
            uniform token type = "linear"
            uniform token purpose = "guide"
        }

        # Pad-to-pad line: two points at finger pad tip positions
        # when FULLY OPEN. The segment length should equal
        # gripper_maxOpening.
        def BasisCurves "gripper_grip_line"
        {
            point3f[] points = [(-0.0425, 0, 0.05), (0.0425, 0, 0.05)]
            int[] curveVertexCounts = [2]
            uniform token type = "linear"
            uniform token purpose = "guide"
        }
    }

Test exceeded its declared max_duration of 300 seconds; the engine session was terminated (retries exhausted).

MJC skipped: asset has only 1/10 joints with finite position limits; MJC needs at least 2.

WHAT THE TEST FOUND:
  - Articulation DOFs reported by Isaac: 10
  - DOFs with finite (lower, upper) and upper-lower > 1e-6: 1
  - Required by MJC: >= 2 (each driven independently to a mid-range
    target chosen by target_factors x [lower+margin, upper-margin]).

WHY IT MATTERS:
  MJC validates simultaneous multi-joint convergence under the PD
  drive controller. A revolute joint authored without limits (or
  with type='none', or as a continuous joint) has no mid-range
  target the test can pick, so it cannot participate.

FIX: On every joint you intend MJC to exercise, author finite
position limits on the matching axis. For PhysicsRevoluteJoint use
lowerLimit/upperLimit in DEGREES; for PhysicsPrismaticJoint use
lowerLimit/upperLimit in the stage's linear unit (typically meters).
Both must be finite and upperLimit > lowerLimit.

TEMPLATE -- paste/edit on each joint prim. Pick limits that match
the real mechanical travel of the joint; do NOT use +-inf:

    def PhysicsRevoluteJoint "joint_1"
    {
        uniform token physics:axis = "Z"
        float physics:lowerLimit = -170.0   # degrees
        float physics:upperLimit =  170.0   # degrees
        # ... body0 / body1 / localPos0 / localPos1 ...
    }

    def PhysicsPrismaticJoint "slider_1"
    {
        uniform token physics:axis = "X"
        float physics:lowerLimit = 0.0      # meters
        float physics:upperLimit = 0.085    # meters
        # ... body0 / body1 / localPos0 / localPos1 ...
    }

CHECKLIST per joint you expect MJC to drive:
  - physics:axis is set (X / Y / Z).
  - physics:lowerLimit and physics:upperLimit are BOTH finite.
  - physics:upperLimit - physics:lowerLimit > 1e-6 (non-degenerate).
  - Joint is reachable from the articulation root (otherwise Isaac
    will not expose it as a DOF; see FET_024 for articulation
    topology requirements).

If the joint is intentionally free-running (e.g. a passive wheel),
exclude it from your articulation rather than leaving it limit-less.

VEL: 1/1 joint(s) exceeded their authored velocity limit: finger_joint.

What the test did:
  - Commanded each joint to the opposite end of its position
    range (with a 5% margin) and stepped physics for
    `test_duration_seconds` (default 2s) at `physics_fps` (default 240).
  - Compared the per-frame |joint velocity| (rad/s) against the
    authored velocity limit, converted from its USD units
    (degrees/s for revolute, distance/s for prismatic) to rad/s,
    allowing a `tolerance_percent` overshoot (default 5%).

Per-joint peaks:
    - finger_joint: peak=4.158, limit=1.175 (+253.7% over, limit-source=dof_or_usd_min)

FIX -- decide which side is wrong and edit the asset:

(a) If the joint legitimately needs to move that fast, raise
    the authored limit on the joint prim to match the
    datasheet rated speed:

        over <./Robot/joints/finger_joint>:
        {
            # New value >= observed peak, authored in DEGREES/s
            # (revolute) or distance/s (prismatic). The peak
            # reported above is rad/s -- multiply by 180/pi to
            # get deg/s. Keep within physical limits.
            float physxJoint:maxJointVelocity = <new_value>
        }

(b) If the limit is correct and the drive is overshooting,
    retune the PD controller on the joint's drive so it
    cannot accelerate past the cap when chasing the target:
      - LOWER `drive:angular:physics:stiffness` (or
        `drive:linear:physics:stiffness`).
      - RAISE `drive:*:physics:damping`.
      - LOWER `drive:*:physics:maxForce` -- excess available
        torque is what lets the joint blow past the cap.
    A reasonable starting point: damping ~= 2 * sqrt(stiffness
    * effective_inertia); then iterate.

(c) If both the limit and the drive are correct and PhysX is
    still overshooting by a small margin, bump
    `tolerance_percent` in the test config -- but only as a
    last resort; (a) and (b) are the right fix.

Per-joint peak velocities are also recorded as warnings above
and counted in `vel_joints_failed` in result.json.
